extra.message: confirmPasswordReset() validates the reset token by looking it up with passwordResetTokenRepository.findByToken(token), but then applies the new password to appUserRepository.findByEmail(email) using the caller-supplied 'email' parameter instead of resetToken.user. An attacker can request a password reset for their own account (obtaining a valid, unexpired, unused token), then POST /password-reset/confirm with their own token but the victim's email address, taking over any account by email address alone.

extra.message: The /agency/handover endpoint (permitAll, CSRF-exempt) parses the 'assertion' parameter with Jwts.parser().unsecured().build().parseClaimsJwt(), which accepts unsigned ('alg: none' / plaintext) JWTs with no signature verification. Any anonymous caller can forge an assertion naming any user's email as the subject and be fully authenticated as that user, including PROPERTY_ADMIN, via SecurityContextHolder.setContext().

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: The /agency/registry-updates/{ticketId} endpoint parses the X-Registry-Assertion header with Jwts.parser().unsecured().build().parseClaimsJwt(), which never verifies a signature. Any caller can forge an assertion with an arbitrary subject (e.g. a PROPERTY_ADMIN email) and be authenticated as that user to transition any maintenance ticket.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: The /agency/registry-updates/{ticketId}/triage endpoint parses the X-Registry-Assertion header with the same unsigned-JWT-accepting parser (Jwts.parser().unsecured()), letting an unauthenticated caller impersonate any portal user and drive ticket status via the dispatch assistant.

cwe: CWE-347: Improper Verification of Cryptographic Signature

extra.message: POST /agency/assignments/{ownerRef} is matched by the permitAll '/agency/**' rule in SecurityConfig and has no authentication or authorization check of its own, yet it directly assigns an arbitrary manager (by email) to an arbitrary property via adminUserService.assignManagerFromOwner(). Any unauthenticated caller can grant a chosen manager account control over any property.

cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: renderNotice() compiles the caller-supplied 'noticeBody' string directly as a FreeMarker template with setNewBuiltinClassResolver(TemplateClassResolver.UNRESTRICTED_RESOLVER), which allows FreeMarker's '?new()' built-in to instantiate arbitrary Java classes. Reachable via GET /notifications/preview (any authenticated user, header X-Notice-Body), this is a server-side template injection that leads to remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: The X-Notice-Body request header is passed unmodified into notificationService.renderNotice(), which evaluates it as a FreeMarker template with an unrestricted class resolver, giving any authenticated user remote code execution via SSTI payloads such as '${"freemarker.template.utility.Execute"?new()("id")}'.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: searchByMethod() builds a native SQL query by directly concatenating the user-supplied 'method' parameter into the query string ("... AND p.method = '" + method + "'") instead of using a bind parameter, allowing SQL injection via GET /payments/search?method=.

cwe: CWE-89: SQL Injection

extra.message: convertFormat() builds a shell command by concatenating the client-supplied 'targetFormat' parameter (POST /documents/{id}/convert) directly into a string passed to ProcessBuilder("sh", "-c", ...), with no validation or escaping. A value such as '; rm -rf / #' or '$(...)' executes arbitrary OS commands.

cwe: CWE-78: OS Command Injection

extra.message: importFromSource() passes the client-supplied 'sourceUrl' (POST /documents/retrieve, param 'source') straight to restTemplate.getForEntity() with no host/scheme allowlist, letting an authenticated user make the server fetch arbitrary internal or cloud-metadata URLs (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/, internal admin panels) and return/store the response as a document.

cwe: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)

extra.message: readArchived() URL-decodes the caller-supplied path and reads File(baseDir, decoded) with no canonicalization/containment check (unlike resolveForDownload() below it, which does check). Reached via GET /documents/archive/{storedName}, which also has no @PreAuthorize and never calls AuthorizationService. A path like '..%2F..%2F..%2Fetc%2Fpasswd' lets any authenticated user read arbitrary files on the server.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: archivePreview() has no @PreAuthorize and calls documentService.readArchived() directly, bypassing AuthorizationService.assertCanAccessDocument() that every other document-reading path in DocumentService goes through. Any authenticated user (any role) can read any stored file by guessing/enumerating its stored name, independent of document ownership.

cwe: CWE-862: Missing Authorization

extra.message: storeCompletionEvidence() uses the client-supplied multipart filename (file.originalFilename) unsanitized in evidenceDir.resolve(originalName). A crafted filename containing '../' segments (or an absolute path, which File.resolve() honors verbatim, discarding evidenceDir) lets an authenticated worker/manager/admin write the uploaded file outside the intended ticket-evidence directory, i.e. arbitrary file write.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: importRentEscalations() reads the 'expression' column from an uploaded CSV row and evaluates it with SpEL's StandardEvaluationContext (exprParser.parseExpression(formula).getValue(ctx)), which has no sandboxing and allows calling arbitrary Java methods/types (e.g. T(java.lang.Runtime).getRuntime().exec(...)). A malicious rent-escalation CSV achieves remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: findStaffByUid() builds the LDAP search filter by concatenating the caller-supplied 'uid' directly into the filter string ("(&(objectClass=person)(uid=" + uid + "))") with no escaping of LDAP metacharacters. The 'uid' column of an imported manager-assignments CSV flows here unsanitized, allowing LDAP filter injection to alter the search logic or extract directory data.

cwe: CWE-90: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an LDAP Query ('LDAP Injection')

extra.message: applyPartnerFeeSchedule() loads the client-supplied 'schedule' YAML body with loaderOptions.tagInspector = TagInspector { true }, which disables SnakeYaml's default tag restrictions and lets the document instantiate arbitrary Java types via YAML tags (e.g. !!javax.script.ScriptEngineManager), a well-known SnakeYAML remote-code-execution deserialization gadget chain.

cwe: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data

extra.message: fieldSummary() concatenates the client-controlled FIELD_UNIT_FILTER cookie directly into an XPath expression ("//inspection[unit='" + unitFilter + "']") passed to XPath.compile(). A value such as "' or '1'='1" alters the query logic, and boolean-based blind XPath injection can be used to exfiltrate inspection data beyond the user's own unit.

cwe: CWE-643: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions ('XPath Injection')

extra.message: unitRegistry() concatenates the client-controlled X-Unit-Ref header directly into an XPath expression ("//unit[unitNumber='" + unitRef + "']/property") evaluated with XPath.evaluate(). This allows XPath injection to manipulate the query and potentially disclose property names for units outside the caller's assigned properties.

cwe: CWE-643: Improper Neutralization of Data within XPath Expressions ('XPath Injection')

extra.message: statusCard() writes raw HTML built by string concatenation of the X-Embed-Label request header and ticket.title (itself tenant-supplied when the ticket was created) with no HTML-escaping, directly to the response body as text/html. This is both a reflected XSS (via the header) and a stored XSS (via the ticket title) on an endpoint meant to be embedded by partner marketing sites.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: partnerSiteCorsFilter() sets setAllowedOriginPatterns(listOf("*")) together with allowCredentials = true for /api/reference/**, which reflects any requesting origin while allowing credentialed (cookie-bearing) cross-origin requests. Any malicious website can issue authenticated requests to /api/reference/** on behalf of a logged-in portal user and read the JSON response (e.g. partner/unit-summary data).
